domain_label: Enrollment Periods, Plan Comparison & Needs Fit
purpose: How a certified agent determines which enrollment window a beneficiary is actually in, turns that person's own doctors, medications, existing coverage and cost tolerance into a documented need-driven comparison of coverage routes, and runs an enrollment conversation in which the beneficiary rather than the agent, the family or the compensation schedule makes the election.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the agent is individually licensed for the relevant lines in the client's state and holds current plan-year certifications and carrier appointments; those requirement classes themselves are owned by the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB and are treated here only as a precondition to check

window dates, plan designs, formularies, provider networks, penalty construction and compensation schedules change every plan year and vary by state and county, so every specific in this KB is a class to be verified against the current-year official source for that client, never a fact recited from memory
this KB is educational and operational; it does not substitute for personalized insurance, medical, tax or legal advice, and the election belongs to the beneficiary

most clients are seniors and some are situationally or cognitively vulnerable, so comprehension and ethical-contact constraints are treated as design requirements of the process rather than courtesies layered on top

no dollar amounts, premium levels, penalty amounts, subsidy thresholds or commission figures are asserted anywhere; money is described as a mechanism whose current values are looked up per case and dated in the file
exclusions: the certification, licensing and carrier-appointment stack itself, the CMS marketing-rule classes, permission-to-contact and scope-of-appointment wording and retention, compliant lead generation and community presence, and audit-surviving documentation habits in general - the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB owns all of that; this KB only checks that those artifacts exist before the enrollment work starts

renewal-compensation mechanics, the year-round service model, mid-year plan-change and provider-issue service, annual-review practice, retention and compliant referral growth - the renewal-compensation-service-and-retention KB owns those; this KB stops at a verified, documented, effective enrollment handed over
personalized plan recommendations: this KB describes how to compare, verify and document, never which plan a named person should buy
medical, clinical, pharmacological, tax or legal advice, including whether a specific treatment will be covered or whether a client should change a medication

specific premium amounts, cost-sharing amounts, penalty amounts, subsidy income thresholds, commission figures and calendar dates, all of which are plan-year and jurisdiction specific and must be looked up in the official current-year source

employer-group benefit administration, union and retiree plan administration, and marketplace subsidy determination beyond recognizing the class and routing the client to the administrator or official source
carrier-side underwriting decisions, claims adjudication, appeals representation and anything that constitutes acting as the client's legal representative
using compensation differences between product classes as a reason, stated or unstated, to prefer one option in any comparison shown to a client

competency_questions.question: Which enrollment window is this person actually in right now, what change does it allow, and when would that change take effect?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENROLLMENT_WINDOW_TAXONOMY names the window class, the change it permits and its effective-date rule, and ELIGIBILITY_PATHWAY_MAP supplies the eligibility basis and anchor dates the window hangs on, both verified against the current plan-year source

competency_questions.question: What has to be true before I am allowed to have this conversation at all, and what exactly am I telling the client I am and am not doing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMISSION_AND_APPOINTMENT_PRECONDITION gives the readiness gate on permission, scope, licensure and appointment, and EDUCATIONAL_ROLE_BOUNDARY gives the spoken role-and-limited-carrier disclosure and the referral map for questions outside scope

competency_questions.question: What must I know about this person before any plan name is spoken, and how do I capture it so a later recommendation is defensible as need-driven?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEEDS_INTAKE_DOSSIER lists the fact classes gathered and the written artifact they produce, including the must-keep ranking recorded in the client's own words

competency_questions.question: What coverage does this person already hold, what happens to it if they enroll, and where is the gap that creates a late-enrollment charge?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_COVERAGE_AUDIT classifies the existing coverage and states who confirms in writing whether it can be kept, dropped or resumed, and CREDITABLE_COVERAGE_AND_LATE_PENALTY_CLASS describes the surcharge mechanism and the evidence the client must keep

competency_questions.question: How do I find out whether this client qualifies for assistance that changes both what they should buy and which windows they have, without prejudging them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUAL_ELIGIBLE_AND_ASSISTANCE_SCREENING names the assistance classes to screen for, the respectful way to ask, and the official application paths the client is routed to

competency_questions.question: How do the two main coverage architectures actually work, and which parts of that choice are hard to undo later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_ROUTE_ARCHITECTURE explains both routes as payment, access and cost-shape mechanisms without ranking them, and SUPPLEMENT_UNDERWRITING_WINDOW_CLASS states the guaranteed-acceptance window asymmetry and the state-variation warning

competency_questions.question: How do I check this client's own doctors and prescriptions against a candidate plan without turning a directory entry into a promise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVIDER_NETWORK_VERIFICATION specifies the two-source check, the dated record and the language that keeps it a check rather than a guarantee, and DRUG_LIST_FIT_ANALYSIS specifies the per-drug tier and utilization-management review plus pharmacy status

competency_questions.question: How do I show what a plan will really cost this person over a year without inventing numbers or reducing it to the lowest premium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOTAL_COST_EXPOSURE_MODEL separates fixed cost, expected cost-sharing, drug-phase cost and worst-case ceiling, sources every figure to a dated current-year lookup, and presents ranges with the driving assumption named

competency_questions.question: How do I keep the shortlist honestly driven by this client's needs when the options do not all pay me the same?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_DRIVEN_COMPARISON_SET states the assembly rules including the do-nothing baseline and the named-gap rule, and COMPENSATION_NEUTRALITY_CONTROL states the criteria-first sequence, the written rationale and the book-skew self-audit

competency_questions.question: How do I run the meeting so the beneficiary genuinely makes the decision, including when a family member is pushing or the client is struggling to follow?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANT_ENROLLMENT_CONVERSATION gives the order of the meeting and the comprehension check, and VULNERABLE_CONSUMER_CARE gives the pacing, representative, stop and no-pressure rules

competency_questions.question: What has to be right at submission, and how do I confirm the person is actually covered on the date they think they are?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENROLLMENT_APPLICATION_EXECUTION covers window-code selection, identifier accuracy, required consent artifacts and effective-date confirmation, and POST_SUBMISSION_VERIFICATION covers acceptance, card, prior-coverage and first-fill checks with an escalation path

competency_questions.question: What file must exist afterward so a third party could reconstruct this enrollment a year later, and what is handed to the service side?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARTIFACT_AND_DOCUMENTATION_PACK enumerates the retained artifacts and the client's own copy, and HANDOFF_TO_SERVICE_YEAR states the exit criteria and the packet the service practice receives

competency_questions.question: What do I do when the calendar has already gone wrong - a missed window, a weak special-window claim, or an election that produced the wrong result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WINDOW_MISS_AND_REMEDY_PATHS maps the remedy classes and their consequences, routes to the program's own exception process and the neutral counseling program, and states the prohibition on manufacturing or coaching a qualifying event

competency_questions.question: How do I get through the annual window without letting volume degrade the quality of any single enrollment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_CAPACITY_PLANNING gives the load forecast, the pre-season work that leaves the peak, the daily appointment ceiling and the stated cut-off that pushes work to the next slot instead of compressing a meeting

glossary.definition: A named category of period during which a beneficiary is permitted to make a specific kind of coverage election; each class differs in who qualifies, what change is allowed and when the resulting coverage begins, and each is verified per case against the current plan-year source rather than recalled.

The window class that opens around a person's first eligibility and is anchored to their eligibility event rather than to the calendar; it is the one time most beneficiaries can enter any route with the fewest conditions attached.

The recurring fall window in which most beneficiaries may change plans for the following coverage year; it concentrates the year's plan-change work into a few weeks and drives the seasonal capacity problem.

A window class opened by a documented qualifying event - moving out of a service area, losing employer or other creditable coverage, a plan contract change, a change in assistance status - whose qualification must be evidenced, never assumed or coached.

Prior coverage that the rules treat as good enough to avoid a late-enrollment charge for the relevant program part; whether a given plan counts is determined by the plan's own notice and the current rules, not by the agent's judgment.

A limited period or triggering situation in which a supplement carrier must issue a policy without medical underwriting; outside it, most states allow underwriting, which is what makes leaving the supplement route a decision that may not be reversible.

The list that says whether a plan covers a drug, at what cost tier, and under what conditions - prior authorization, step therapy or quantity limits - all of which are set per plan and per year and must be checked against the client's actual prescriptions.

An annual ceiling on a member's cost-sharing that exists in some coverage architectures and not in others; its presence or absence is the single clearest way to describe worst-case exposure without quoting a number.
The client's current arrangement carried into the comparison as an explicit option, so that changing plans has to earn its place against staying put rather than being assumed.

A provider, facility or medication the client has stated they will not give up, recorded in writing at intake and ranked before any plan is named, so that a later failure to satisfy it is visible rather than quietly traded away.

nodes.definition: Before a single needs question is asked, settle whether this contact may happen and whether this agent can actually transact for this person: the beneficiary's permission-to-contact record covers the channel being used, a scope-of-appointment-class artifact exists for the product lines about to be discussed and has satisfied its timing rule, the agent's license is active for the client's state and lines, and the current plan-year certifications and carrier appointments cover every plan that could plausibly come up in the comparison. This node owns only the yes/no readiness answer that sits at the top of the enrollment file and the rule that an unready agent reschedules rather than improvises; the wording, timing, retention and audit form of those artifacts belong to the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB. Readiness is checked per carrier and per state, not once per season, because an agent can be fully certified and still unappointed for the one plan a client asks about.

included: the pre-meeting readiness check covering permission, scope artifact, state licensure and per-carrier appointment
the reschedule-instead-of-proceed rule and the script for it
recording the readiness result at the top of the enrollment file
excluded: the regulatory wording, timing rules and retention periods of the permission and scope artifacts, which the certifications-and-marketing KB owns
how leads that produced the contact were generated
annual recertification cadence and carrier contracting mechanics

pros.claim: Catching an appointment or licensure gap before the meeting prevents an application that cannot be submitted for the plan the client chose
pros.example: discovering during the readiness check that the carrier whose network holds the client's cardiologist is one the agent is not appointed for, and saying so at the start instead of after a two-hour comparison

pros.claim: A written readiness result gives the file a defensible first page when the enrollment is reviewed later
pros.example: a reviewer opening the file and seeing the scope artifact reference and appointment status dated before the meeting rather than reconstructed afterward

cons.claim: The gate can cost a live opportunity when a client is ready to talk and the paperwork is not yet in place
cons.example: a walk-in during the annual window who has to be booked for a later day because the scope artifact for the product line has not aged as required

cons.claim: Per-carrier checking is tedious and tempts agents into a once-per-season assumption that goes stale mid-year
cons.example: assuming a carrier appointment carried over when the carrier added a mid-year condition the agent never completed

failure_modes: starting a needs conversation on a channel the client never gave permission for
discussing a product line outside the agreed scope because the client raised it
comparing a plan the agent is not appointed to sell and then steering the client away from it to hide the gap
treating a season-opening certification sweep as proof of readiness for every carrier all year
acceptance_tests: the file records, dated before the meeting, that permission covers the channel used, a scope artifact covers the lines discussed, the license is active in the client's state, and each carrier whose plans may be shown is one the agent is appointed for
any readiness gap is recorded together with what was done about it - reschedule, restricted scope, or referral out
revisit_triggers: a carrier adds or changes an appointment or certification condition mid-year
the client asks to discuss a product line outside the agreed scope
the client moves to another state or the meeting channel changes

base.update_signal: a change in marketing-rule requirements for permission or scope artifacts, or a carrier changing its appointment and certification conditions for the plan year

nodes.definition: Say out loud, at the start and again whenever the conversation drifts, what the agent is doing and what the agent is not doing. The agent explains how coverage routes work, checks the client's own doctors and prescriptions against current-year plan sources, lays out trade-offs in both directions and writes down what was shown. The agent does not predict the client's future health, does not give medical, tax or legal advice, does not decide for the client, and discloses plainly that they represent a limited set of carriers rather than every plan available in the area. This is a working boundary, not a slogan: it determines how the inevitable 'just tell me which one you would pick' is answered, what a comparison sheet is allowed to claim, and where the conversation is routed outward - to the plan's own coverage documents, to the prescriber or pharmacist, to the official program source, or to the state health insurance counseling program that has no product to sell.

included: the spoken opening that names the agent's role, the limited-carrier disclosure and who makes the election
the answer pattern for the pick-one-for-me question that returns to the client's own recorded criteria
the outward referral map for questions past the boundary
excluded: the regulatory form and timing of required disclosures, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB
clinical judgment about the client's care or medications
household financial, tax or estate planning

pros.claim: Stating the boundary in minute one turns a later refusal to choose for the client into a kept promise rather than an evasion
pros.example: a client who was told at the start that the decision is theirs accepts a two-sided trade-off summary at the end instead of pressing for a directive

pros.claim: A named referral map keeps the agent useful at the edge of scope instead of improvising an answer that is not theirs to give
pros.example: routing 'will my knee replacement be covered' to the plan's coverage documents and the carrier's coverage-determination process rather than guessing

cons.claim: Clients often experience the boundary as unhelpfulness and some will go to whoever sounds more certain
cons.example: a client leaving for an agent who says 'this is the best plan, sign here' and only discovering the network problem in March

cons.claim: Holding the line lengthens meetings, which collides directly with annual-window capacity
cons.example: spending twenty minutes explaining that the agent cannot promise a specific surgery is covered, during the busiest week of the year

failure_modes: sliding from explaining trade-offs into telling the client what to buy because it saves time
answering a coverage question definitively when only the plan document can answer it
omitting the limited-carrier disclosure so the client believes they have seen the whole market
letting an educational frame become a shield for saying nothing useful at all
acceptance_tests: the opening disclosure - role, limited-carrier fact, and who makes the election - is recorded in the file for every enrollment contact
every out-of-scope question in the notes has a recorded destination: plan document, prescriber or pharmacist, official program source, or counseling program
revisit_triggers: a client says they understood the agent to be recommending or choosing for them
the agent's carrier lineup changes, altering what the limited-carrier disclosure must say
a complaint or review names the advice boundary

base.update_signal: a regulator, carrier or complaint record clarifies where education ends and personalized recommendation begins for agents in this channel

nodes.definition: Treat the fact that this book is mostly seniors, some of them cognitively or situationally vulnerable, as a constraint on how the whole process is built rather than as a bedside manner. Concretely: pace the meeting to the client rather than the calendar, check comprehension by asking the client to state the trade-off back in their own words, establish early whether a spouse, adult child or power-of-attorney-class representative is present and in what role, and record that. Impose rules on the agent's own behaviour - no urgency the agent manufactured, no fear framing about what could happen if they do not act today, no exploiting a deadline that does not actually apply to this client, no election taken while the client is distressed or unwell. Recognize the signs that a client cannot presently make the decision and stop the meeting rather than proceeding with a signature, and refuse to take an election a family member wants and the beneficiary has not chosen.

included: pacing, plain-language rewording and the restate-it-back comprehension check
identifying and documenting an authorized representative's role and authority
the agent's self-imposed no-pressure rules and the stop-the-meeting criteria
excluded: clinical assessment of capacity, which the agent is not qualified to make
legal determination of guardianship or authority, which is routed to the family's own counsel
the regulatory text of prohibited marketing practices, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB

pros.claim: A comprehension check catches misunderstandings before they become an election the client would not have made
pros.example: asking a client to explain in their own words what happens if they use a doctor outside the network, and discovering they thought the plan would still pay the same

pros.claim: Documenting who else was in the room protects both the beneficiary and the agent when a relative later disputes the enrollment
pros.example: a note that the daughter attended by speakerphone at the client's request and that the client answered every election question herself

cons.claim: Slower, stop-if-in-doubt meetings reduce how many enrollments an agent can complete in the peak weeks
cons.example: rescheduling a confused client into January-adjacent capacity that is already scarce during the annual window

cons.claim: Judging whether a client can decide today is a judgment the agent is not trained to make and can be wrong in both directions
cons.example: reading a hard-of-hearing client's slow responses as confusion and delaying a decision they were perfectly able to make

failure_modes: accepting a nodding client as an understanding client
letting a dominant relative answer the questions the beneficiary must answer
using the closing window as emotional leverage rather than as information
taking an election from a client who is clearly unwell or distressed because rescheduling is inconvenient
acceptance_tests: the file records that the client restated the central trade-off in their own words before any election was taken
where anyone other than the beneficiary participated, the file names them, their role and that the beneficiary answered the election questions
no note anywhere in the file cites a deadline or consequence that the agent cannot source to the client's actual window or plan documents
revisit_triggers: the client or a family member later says they did not understand what was chosen
a client shows a change in comprehension between contacts
guidance on protecting vulnerable consumers in this channel is updated

base.update_signal: updated guidance on vulnerable-consumer protection, or a pattern of post-enrollment confusion in the agent's own book

nodes.definition: Establish how this specific person becomes eligible and what dates follow from it, because the pathway - reaching the qualifying age, qualifying through a long-term disability determination class, or qualifying under a specific-condition class - decides which windows open, when they open, and what the person must actively file versus what happens automatically. The work is: confirm the basis from the client's own records rather than their recollection, capture the anchor dates that everything else keys off (entitlement start, birthday month, the month active employment or employer coverage ends), determine whether enrollment in the base program parts is automatic for this person or must be filed with the administering agency and by when, and record the county and permanent residence because plan availability is geographic and a county line can change the entire option set. Anything uncertain is verified against the official source or the client's own award or enrollment documents before it is used.

included: identifying the eligibility basis class and evidencing it from the client's documents
capturing anchor dates and whether base-program enrollment is automatic or must be filed
recording county and permanent residence as the geographic key to plan availability
excluded: adjudicating eligibility, which only the administering agency does
advising on when to claim retirement benefits or how that interacts with taxes

pros.claim: Anchoring on documents rather than recollection prevents a whole comparison keyed to the wrong month
pros.example: a client sure their coverage starts the month of their birthday when their own award letter shows a different entitlement month

pros.claim: Capturing county early prevents building an option set that does not exist at the client's address
pros.example: a client living just across a county line from the town they name, where the available plan set differs from the one the agent assumed

cons.claim: Clients often cannot find the documents, so the step stalls at the moment enthusiasm is highest
cons.example: an age-in client who cannot locate their program card and must request information before the comparison can proceed

cons.claim: Non-standard pathways carry rules the agent may not have seen recently and cannot safely reconstruct from memory
cons.example: a client who qualified years earlier through a disability determination and is now aging into a different rule set

failure_modes: assuming an age-based pathway for someone who qualified another way
reading the anchor date off the client's memory rather than their card or award letter
missing that a base-program part still has to be actively filed for this person
using a mailing address that differs from the permanent residence that governs plan availability
acceptance_tests: the eligibility basis, anchor dates and county in the file each cite the document or official source they came from, with the date checked
whether base-program enrollment is automatic or must be filed for this person is recorded with the filing deadline where one applies
revisit_triggers: the client's employment, residence or disability status changes
the client produces a document that contradicts the recorded anchor date

base.update_signal: the client's own documents or the administering agency contradict the recorded eligibility basis or anchor dates

nodes.definition: Hold the enrollment-period system as a small set of window classes and, for each, the three things that actually matter in a client conversation: who qualifies, what change it permits, and when the resulting coverage takes effect. The classes are the initial window opening around first eligibility; the recurring annual election window in which most changes for the following coverage year are made; the additional open-enrollment window class available to someone already enrolled in an advantage-class plan, which permits a narrower set of changes; the general-enrollment window class for people who did not enrol when first eligible, which carries its own effective-date and surcharge consequences; and the special window classes opened by documented qualifying events such as a permanent move out of a service area, loss of employer or other creditable coverage, a plan contract or service-area change, or a change in assistance-program status. The taxonomy is also the business's demand calendar: it explains why the year has one enormous peak and a steady trickle of age-in and event-driven work around it. Dates, qualification detail and effective-date rules are verified for the current plan year per case, never quoted from last year's memory.

included: the window classes and the qualify / permitted-change / effective-date triple for each
matching a specific client's situation to exactly one window class and evidencing the match
the demand-calendar consequence: annual peak plus year-round age-in and event work
excluded: asserting current-year calendar dates, which are looked up per plan year
the remedy work when no window applies, which the remedy-paths node owns
renewal and annual-review service, owned by the renewal-service KB

pros.claim: Matching a client to exactly one window class turns a vague 'can I switch' into a concrete answer with an effective date
pros.example: telling a client who just moved permanently that a special window class applies from the move, and what evidence of the move the carrier will want

pros.claim: Knowing the effective-date rule per window prevents the most common client shock, which is a gap between signing and being covered
pros.example: an election made in one window taking effect the following month while the client assumed it started immediately

cons.claim: The class boundaries are genuinely intricate and a confident wrong answer is worse than a checked one
cons.example: treating a change of address within the same service area as a qualifying move when it may not open any window

cons.claim: Concentrating most permitted change into one annual window creates a demand peak that stresses every quality control in the process
cons.example: a book where nearly all plan changes must be discussed, verified and submitted inside a few weeks

failure_modes: telling a client they can change plans whenever they like
reusing last plan year's dates or rules without re-verification
claiming a special window on an event class that does not actually qualify
confusing the window in which an election is made with the date coverage begins
acceptance_tests: the file names the window class relied on, the evidence that the client qualifies for it, the change it permits, and the effective date it produces
every window date or rule used in the conversation cites a current plan-year source with the date it was checked
revisit_triggers: the plan year turns over or the program publishes updated window rules
the client's circumstances change in a way that could open or close a window
a carrier or the program disputes the window code used on a submitted application

base.update_signal: the program publishes plan-year window rules or dates that differ from the ones the agent has been using

nodes.definition: Run a structured intake that produces, in writing and before any plan is named, the facts the entire comparison will be built on: the medication list exactly as the client takes it including strength and quantity rather than as they remember the brand; the doctors, specialists and hospitals they intend to keep, each marked must-keep or nice-to-keep in the client's own words; chronic conditions only so far as they predict utilization, never as clinical assessment; travel patterns, snowbird arrangements and second residences; whether they are willing to accept referral and prior-authorization steps in exchange for lower fixed cost; budget tolerance expressed both as a comfortable monthly amount and as the worst month they could absorb; and any other coverage or assistance already held. The dossier is signed off verbally with the client - read back and corrected - because it is the artifact that later makes a recommendation defensible as need-driven rather than product-driven.

included: the medication list with strengths and quantities as actually taken
the provider list with a must-keep versus nice-to-keep ranking recorded in the client's words
utilization, travel, tolerance for referral steps and two-sided budget tolerance
the read-back that confirms the dossier before comparison begins
excluded: clinical interpretation of conditions or medications
verification against plan sources, which the network and formulary nodes own
any discussion of specific plans, which comes only after the dossier is fixed

pros.claim: Fixing must-keep constraints in writing before plans are named makes later steering visible and prevents constraint drift
pros.example: a client who said in week one that their oncologist is non-negotiable, so an otherwise attractive plan that excludes that practice is shown as failing rather than quietly dropped from view

pros.claim: Exact strengths and quantities are what make the drug analysis meaningful at all
pros.example: the same medication at a different strength landing on a different tier and changing which option is cheapest across the year

cons.claim: A thorough intake is long and can exhaust an older client before the comparison even starts
cons.example: forty minutes of prescriptions and providers leaving no attention left for the trade-off discussion, forcing a second meeting

cons.claim: Clients under-report - occasional drugs, a specialist they see yearly, a spouse's plan - and the gap surfaces only after enrollment
cons.example: a quarterly injection never mentioned because the client does not think of it as a prescription

failure_modes: naming a plan before the dossier exists, which anchors everything that follows
recording drug names without strength, quantity or how often they are actually taken
not distinguishing must-keep from nice-to-keep, so every provider becomes negotiable under pressure
letting a family member supply the answers about the beneficiary's own care
acceptance_tests: the dossier exists in the file, is dated before any plan was named, and was read back to the client and corrected
each provider carries a must-keep or nice-to-keep marking and each medication carries strength and quantity as taken
revisit_triggers: the client reports a new prescription, a new specialist or a change of pharmacy
a verification step contradicts something the dossier records
more than one plan year has passed since the dossier was refreshed

base.update_signal: post-enrollment problems trace back to a fact class the intake never asked about
